# `save_stack`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Save the current stack result to storage using the stored save settings.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd0fc0, SaveStack @0x1929e0 (64-bit build) |

Builds the stack image name and header, obtains or computes the stacked image and starts the save thread without waiting for it. Acquisition and conversion are synchronous; the file write is asynchronous, so a success reply does not mean the file exists. The destination and type come from stored save/autosave settings; request parameters (path, type) are not read. The call needs an accumulated image but does not open hardware. It refuses the simulated stack and unsupported capture types. On error 213 the reply may carry an additional top-level fullname string when a non-empty saved file name is known. Completion events and deeper file/SDK failures are unresolved.

Side effects: Starts an asynchronous write of the stacked image and its header to the currently selected storage; may compute calibration or fetch the stacked frame.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"save_stack"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (success) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (success) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 300 | Internal frame type is 4 | `internal error` |
| 267 | The light stack has no positive frame count | `no image` |
| 213 | The image is already saved; the reply may include fullname | `image is already saved` |
| 207 | Fallback when a failure leaves no code | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Failures from buffer reallocation, calibration calculation, stacked-frame retrieval and starting the save thread are forwarded unchanged and are not enumerated. A simulated stack, or a non-zero capture type other than star trails, makes the call return failure without assigning a new code, so the code is whatever was last set (207 if none).

## Example

Request, save:

```json
{"id":71,"method":"save_stack"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"save_stack","result":0,"code":0,"id":71}
```

Reply, nothing-stacked:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"save_stack","error":"no image","code":267,"id":72}
```

Reply, already-saved:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"save_stack","error":"image is already saved","code":213,"id":73,"fullname":"Example_stack_20260131"}
```
